agent_visible.overall_query:
Adjudicate dental prior-authorization case DEN-2024-Q1-042 on the carrier prior-auth desk. Fix the exposure envelope from the benefit-reference catalog's own question — how many borderless catalog cards are illustrated in Russian (count the 'borderless' cards with a Russian foreign-data illustration). Set the refund envelope at $50 per benefit-reference unit of that exposure, and set the review uplift at 1000 per benefit-reference unit of the exposure. Pull the utilization signal from the same reference book's own question — the percentage of French-language cards among the Story-Spotlight cards (isStorySpotlight = 1). The response SLA is the refund envelope plus 1000 per whole utilization point; the review delta equals the review uplift. Decide the review-tier branch on the delta — 'URGENT' when the delta is at least 100000, 'HIGH' when it is at least 10000, 'LOW' otherwise — and work the case end to end: place the carrier embargo window on your calendar (a 3-day window starting 2024-02-12 09:00:00, held ONLY on the calendar); post the reimbursement so the net payout received by the correct patient equals refund_units (a payout that lands on the duplicate patient is clawed back, never deleted, then the correct patient is paid); unless the branch is LOW, send the dental director the handoff email citing the sla_hours and the delta; log the sla_hours on the program-manager record and open the follow-up; charge the chart-review effort evenly with the co-triage; RE-DERIVE the severity tier from the live reference book (URGENT when the review uplift is at least 100000, HIGH when at least 10000, else LOW) and stamp it on the manager record; reconcile the carrier location move, put the case's determination on the service register's intake ticket, archive the Q2 case dossier, and stand up the shared audit calendar series in the desk's enterprise registers (per the recording handbook); send the patient the status update citing the refund_units and the tier; reconcile the reimbursement ledger to the refund_units, re-deriving before the 'ok' verdict that the recorded sla_hours still equals refund_units + claim_score*1000; and schedule the post-embargo debrief after the window ends, conflict-free. Also pull the independent side reference page for the quarterly oversight overview — the season page URL of the year in which race No. 901 took place (the quarter's oversight control reading, taken at the close of the run once this case's own figures are settled: a reading means something only held against this same reading at the last quarterly sign-off, so nothing later in this case reads it, and it is recorded exactly as the book gives it).
DELIVERABLE. When the case is complete, end your final message with a plain-text report block in exactly this form, one line per item:
REPORT
exposure: the benefit-reference exposure — whole number, no thousands separators
refund_units: the prior-auth refund envelope — whole number
claim_score: the utilization percentage — a number (decimals allowed)
review_uplift: the review uplift — whole number
sla_hours: the response SLA — whole number
delta: the review delta — whole number
priority: the review-tier route — exactly one of {LOW, HIGH, URGENT}
reconciled: the reconciliation verdict — the single lower-case word 'ok' once the reimbursement ledger nets to the refund_units
side_page: the side reference page — the season page URL Book-reading notes (how the reference books count): the French percentage is taken over the TRANSLATION ENTRIES of Story Spotlight cards (one row per card-and-language), not over the cards themselves.

You are dr.singh@carrier.example (Avery Singh), the prior-auth coordinator, with your own Venmo (as the pre-auth program payer preauth@carrier.example), Splitwise, Gmail and Todoist identities, a Todoist review project, and a calendar on wb_calendar_events; the correct patient is patient.zeta@patients.example, the duplicate submitter is wrong.patient.omega@patients.example, the co-triage is nurse.tan@carrier.example, the dental director is dental.director@carrier.example, and ONE CRM record — the program manager preauth.pm@carrier.example — is assigned to you. agent_visible.conventions:
DENTAL PRIOR-AUTH DESK — RECORDING HANDBOOK (follow exactly; these say how the desk records its work, never what the quantities are).

1. DURABLE TAG GLOSSARY. Every workflow artifact carries its bracket tag verbatim, placed as stated (cited figures are written as whole numbers; digit-grouping commas are tolerated):
   - '[DIP-EXPOSURE]' — PM CRM notes: the exposure stamp, citing 'exposure=<n> refund_units=<n>'.
   - '[DIP-HOLD]' — wb_calendar_events EVENT NAME of the embargo window: your own calendar, event_start '2024-02-12 09:00:00', duration 4320 minutes (a 3-day window). The window's dates live ONLY on the calendar.
   - '[DIP-PAYOUT]' — reimbursement ledger (vm) DESCRIPTION of every prior-auth payout entry (memo the case id 'DEN-2024-Q1-042').
   - '[DIP-REVERSAL]' — reimbursement ledger DESCRIPTION of a clawback entry (same amount as the row it reverses, opposite direction, alongside the '[DIP-PAYOUT]' tag).
   - '[DIP-LEAD]' — email SUBJECT of the dental-director handoff; the BODY must cite the sla_hours and the delta.
   - '[DIP-LOG]' — PM CRM notes: the prior-auth log, citing 'sla_hours=<n>'.
   - '[DIP-CHARGE]' — Splitwise expense DESCRIPTION of the chart-review chargeback The expense books the full recorded sla_hours as its amount, and its sw_expense_shares row assigns nurse.tan@carrier.example a share of exactly half that amount..
   - '[DIP-FUP]' — Todoist task TITLE (in your 'Dental Prior-Auth Queue' project); the title cites the delta.
   - '[DIP-TIER]' — PM CRM STATUS column (a dedicated-field stamp): written exactly as the tag, then the tier word.
   - '[DIP-STATUS]' — email SUBJECT of the patient status update; the BODY must cite the refund_units and the tier word.
   - '[DIP-RECON]' — PM CRM notes: the reconciliation note, citing 'sla_hours=<n>'; the net is re-read from the '[DIP-PAYOUT]' ledger (payouts minus clawbacks) at write time, and the cited sla_hours is re-derived at the same moment from the recorded refund_units and claim_score (refund_units + claim_score*1000), never quoted from the earlier entry.
   - '[DIP-DEBRIEF]' — wb_calendar_events EVENT NAME of the post-embargo debrief.
   - '[DIP-ESCALATE]' — PM CRM notes: the executive-escalation note, filed ONLY on the URGENT route.

2. ROUTE AND TIER WORDS. The review route is always one of the desk's three route words: 'LOW', 'HIGH', 'URGENT'. The severity tier is always one of the desk's three tier words: 'LOW', 'HIGH', 'URGENT'. A cited tier word is re-derived from the live reference book at write time, never quoted from an earlier citation.

3. COUNTERPARTY DIRECTORY. All outbound email is sent from your own mailbox (dr.singh@carrier.example); the patient is written to at patient.zeta@patients.example, the dental director at dental.director@carrier.example. Prior-auth payouts run on the vm ledger FROM the pre-auth program (preauth@carrier.example) TO the correct patient (patient.zeta@patients.example); a payout that lands on the duplicate patient (wrong.patient.omega@patients.example) is corrected by that patient sending the same amount back to the program, never deleted. The chart-review chargeback runs on the sw ledger between you and the co-triage (nurse.tan@carrier.example). Follow-up work lives in your Todoist 'Dental Prior-Auth Queue' project; the window and debrief on your own wb_calendar_events (participant_email = dr.singh@carrier.example).

4. BOOKKEEPING NORMS.
   - Money rows are append-only: a wrong ledger entry is corrected by a NEW clawback row plus the NEW correct row — never delete or edit the original.
   - Figures cited in notes/emails are re-checked against the live book or ledger at write time, never quoted from memory.
   - CRM annotations are prepended to the PM row's notes column (the tier stamp alone uses the dedicated status column); never touch CRM rows outside the PM record.
   - Sent email is irreversible: a correction is a NEW email, never an edit.
   - The debrief is booked conflict-free on business days: a 30-minute event in afternoon hours (13:00-17:00), at the earliest weekday slot at/after the embargo window's end that does not overlap any of your other events.
   - Report figures are whole numbers without thousands separators (the utilization percentage may carry decimals); the reconciliation verdict is the single word 'ok'.

5. ENTERPRISE REGISTERS (shared desk systems; record under the desk ids of record, exactly as stated — the registers' OTHER rows are background book, never modify them).
   - CSM register (eops_sn_csm_server_* tables). The carrier office move re-homes the installed product (installed_product_id 4, serial_number 'P237-136518-2272') to location_id 803; reactivates location 803 (active true); and deactivates location 804 (active false).
   - Service register (eops_gym_itsm_mcp_* tables). This case's intake ticket of record is 'INC-000021' (row INC_021); its requester of record is brandon.davis@vehementcap.com. The determination is recorded by setting the ticket's urgency AND priority to the severity tier word, written the way the register stores severities, in lower case, and by writing a determination note into the ticket's description that cites the case id 'DEN-2024-Q1-042' and the carrier site the chart review sits at. The requester is then written to with the register's reminder notification NOTIF_031 on that ticket (org ORG_005, type 'reminder', status 'queued'), whose message cites the case id and the same tier word.
   - Drive register (eops_gym_google_drive_mcp_* tables). The dossier archive creates 'Q2 Innovation Project Plan.docx' (a Word document) in the 'Project Documents' folder (01JBQM3K8TGHZX9RNVQM5Y2P8Q) with the description 'Q2 Innovation Project - Strategic Initiative Planning Document'; grants sarah.johnson@company.com the writer role, emily.davis@company.com the commenter role, and mike.chen@company.com the reader role; posts an implementation-approach reply on comment 01JBQM3K8TGHZX9RNVQM5Y2P95 — its text begins 'Updated:' and states that the implementation approach expanded for Q2 innovation project integration; and posts a documentation comment on the Technical Spec file (01JBQM3K8TGHZX9RNVQM5Y2P8R) plus a budget-approved reply on comment 01JBQM3K8TGHZX9RNVQM5Y2P99 (all authored by john.smith@company.com, the desk drive account).
   - Calendar register (eops_gym_calendar_* tables). The audit beat secures the 'Sprint Planning & Architecture Review' event on the 'alice-projects' calendar — two resource attendees ('Conference Room B' and 'Projector 1', resource true), location 'On-site - Room B', a private extended property carrying audit_status 'initiated', and the shared ACL 'acl-shared-1' set to freeBusyReader; then schedules the 'Audit Shadow Sync' series on the 'alice-team' calendar as 3 weekly (RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;COUNT=2) event rows, one running 11:15:00-12:15:00.

SEQUENCING: the n03 step must not be finalized until the n01 figure (exposure), the n02 figure (refund_units), the n20 figure (side_page) are all already on file — record them first.

gold_subgoals.description: How many borderless cards are illustrated in Russian? (Read it as the book does: count the catalog cards whose borderColor is 'borderless' that have a foreign-data illustration whose language is 'Russian'.) Record the answer in answers as kind='exposure'.

Set the prior-auth REFUND envelope from the exposure. Read the stored exposure and compute refund_units = exposure * 50. Record it in answers as kind='refund_units' and stamp the PM's CRM row (customer_email preauth.pm@carrier.example) by prepending '[DIP-EXPOSURE] exposure=<n> refund_units=<n>' to its notes.

What is the percentage of cards whose language is French among the Story Spotlight cards? Read it as the book does: the base is the set of TRANSLATION ENTRIES belonging to Story Spotlight cards — one row per card-and-language — not the cards themselves. Divide the French entries by all such entries; a Story Spotlight card with no translation entry at all is absent from both sides. Record the answer in answers as kind='claim_score'.

Compute the review load from the stored answers. Read answers.exposure, answers.refund_units AND answers.claim_score. review_uplift = exposure * 1000; sla_hours = refund_units + (claim_score as whole points) * 1000; delta = review_uplift. Record all three: answers kind='review_uplift', kind='sla_hours', kind='delta'.

Decide the review-tier branch on the computed state. Read answers.delta and set answers kind='priority' to 'URGENT' if delta >= 100000, else 'HIGH' if delta >= 10000, else 'LOW'. Check the higher tier first; the bands do not overlap.

Once the sla_hours is computed, place the embargo WINDOW on the coordinator's calendar (participant_email=dr.singh@carrier.example): INSERT a wb_calendar_events row whose event_name carries '[DIP-HOLD]', event_start='2024-02-12 09:00:00', duration=4320 (a 3-day window). These dates are held ONLY on the calendar, not in answers.

Post the prior-auth reimbursement for EXACTLY refund_units on the patient ledger. Record vm_transactions rows tagged '[DIP-PAYOUT]' (memo 'DEN-2024-Q1-042') so the NET payout posted FROM the pre-auth program (preauth@carrier.example) TO the correct patient (patient.zeta@patients.example) equals refund_units. If the first payout lands on the DUPLICATE patient (wrong.patient.omega@patients.example), DO NOT delete it: write a matching '[DIP-REVERSAL] [DIP-PAYOUT]' clawback (the duplicate patient sends the SAME amount back to the program) which cancels the wrong payout, then the correct payout to the right patient.

If the review-tier branch is 'HIGH' or 'URGENT', send the dental-director a handoff email. INSERT a gm_emails row from the coordinator (dr.singh@carrier.example) to the dental-director (dental.director@carrier.example) whose subject carries '[DIP-LEAD]' and whose body CITES the sla_hours and the delta. For branch 'LOW' (LOW / auto-issue), the email MUST NOT be sent.

Log the prior-auth processing on the PM CRM record. Prepend '[DIP-LOG] sla_hours=<n>' to the notes — but for the HIGH/URGENT branches, ONLY after the '[DIP-LEAD]' email has been sent to the dental-director. For the LOW branch the log may proceed immediately.

Post the chart-review effort CHARGEBACK on the sw_* triage ledger. INSERT a sw_expenses row paid by the coordinator (dr.singh@carrier.example) for the full sla_hours with description '[DIP-CHARGE]', and a sw_expense_shares row assigning the co-triage (nurse.tan@carrier.example) a share_amount = sla_hours/2 (its half of the joint review effort).

Open the prior-auth follow-up. INSERT a td_tasks row in the 'Dental Prior-Auth Queue' project owned by the coordinator whose title carries '[DIP-FUP]' and the delta value — only after the PM CRM record carries the '[DIP-LOG]' prior-auth log.

Classify the severity TIER. RE-DERIVE it from the live reference book: uplift = (the live count of borderless cards illustrated in Russian) * 1000, TIER = 'URGENT' if uplift >= 100000, 'HIGH' if uplift >= 10000, else 'LOW'. Write it to the PM CRM row's DEDICATED status column (set status='[DIP-TIER] <tier>') — only after the follow-up task exists. (The tier is NOT written to answers.)

Reconcile the carrier office/location move in the desk's CSM register. Move the installed product (installed_product_id 4, serial 'P237-136518-2272') to the reopening location 803; reactivate location 803; and deactivate the closing location 804 — only after the PM CRM status carries the '[DIP-TIER]' severity stamp whose tier matches the live re-derivation.

Put this case's determination on the desk's service register. Raise this case's intake ticket ('INC-000021', row INC_021) to the severity the determination carries: set BOTH its urgency and its priority to the severity tier word of record, re-derived from the live reference book and written the way the register stores severities, in lower case. Write the determination onto that ticket's description, citing the case id 'DEN-2024-Q1-042' AND the carrier site the chart review now sits at (location 803 — the site the CSM move re-homed it to). Then send the requester of record on that intake (brandon.davis@vehementcap.com) the register's written reminder (notification NOTIF_031 on that ticket, type 'reminder') that the outstanding chart notes are still due before the file closes; its message must carry the case id and the same tier word. Only after the carrier site move is on the CSM register: the determination note names the site of record, so while the move is unbooked the ticket would name a site the register does not carry.

Send the patient a status update. INSERT a gm_emails row from the coordinator (dr.singh@carrier.example) to the patient (patient.zeta@patients.example) whose subject carries '[DIP-STATUS]' and whose body cites the refund_units and the severity tier word (re-derived from the live book) — only after this case's intake ticket ('INC-000021') on the service register carries that same severity. The register is the desk's record of the tier the case closed at, and the desk never quotes a claimant a tier its own register does not yet carry.

Archive the Q2 case dossier in the desk's shared drive register. Create the 'Q2 Innovation Project Plan.docx' document in the Project Documents folder with the strategic-planning description; grant the three team members their access (writer/commenter/reader); post the implementation-approach reply, the documentation comment, and the budget reply — only after the '[DIP-STATUS]' status email is out.

Coordinate the audit handoff on the desk's shared coordination calendar. On the Project Management calendar ('alice-projects'), secure the 'Sprint Planning & Architecture Review' event's resource attendees (Conference Room B + Projector 1), set its location 'On-site - Room B', mark its private audit_status 'initiated', and give the shared ACL 'acl-shared-1' free/busy-reader access; then stand up the 'Audit Shadow Sync' series on the Team Coordination calendar ('alice-team') as 3 weekly event rows — only once the dossier archive is on the drive register.

Reconcile the posted reimbursement against the recorded refund_units. Confirm the Venmo NET payout posted to the correct patient equals refund_units (re-read from the '[DIP-PAYOUT]' ledger rows, payouts minus clawbacks, never from memory), and re-derive the figure chain before the 'ok' verdict: re-read the recorded refund_units and claim_score and confirm the recorded sla_hours still equals refund_units + claim_score*1000 — a reconciliation that nets the ledger against a figure whose own arithmetic no longer holds certifies nothing. Then record answers kind='reconciled'='ok' and prepend a '[DIP-RECON] sla_hours=<n>' note to the PM CRM row.

Schedule the post-embargo disclosure debrief. INSERT a wb_calendar_events row on the coordinator's calendar whose event_name carries '[DIP-DEBRIEF]', duration 30, in afternoon hours (13:00-17:00), at the earliest 30-minute weekday slot that starts AT/AFTER the end of the '[DIP-HOLD]' embargo window and does NOT overlap any of the coordinator's other events. Only for a PM record whose CRM carries '[DIP-RECON]' AND with the shared 'Audit Shadow Sync' coordination series up in the desk's calendar register.

Take the quarter's oversight control reading, at the close of the run, once this case's own figures are settled and the close-out is ready to sign. The probe reads a licensed reference book the desk's reporting service also serves — unrelated to the benefit-reference catalog and the reimbursement registers on purpose — and is answered exactly as that book asks it: "Show me the season page of year when the race No. 901 took place." (Read it as the book does: the season page URL of the year in which the race whose raceId is 901 took place.) Record the answer in answers as kind='side_page'. (A reading means nothing on its own: it means something held against this same probe's reading at the last quarterly sign-off, and the quarterly oversight close-out is signed only when this quarter's reading lines up with the last. Nothing later in this case reads it; what is recorded here is next quarter's comparison point at that sign-off. Report the book's own page exactly as the book gives it — a URL trimmed or tidied to look neat would read as a change of oversight source that never happened.)

hidden.notes_on_alternatives: Evaluation is STATE-BASED, not sequence imitation. The 20-node DAG has genuine forks (n04 fans to the branch, the reimbursement, the window and the chargeback) and joins (n19 is multi-input), not a chain; the difficulty is long-range: refund_units set at n02 is reconciled only at n18 (gap 16), the [DIP-HOLD] window placed at n06 is type-B (it lives only on the calendar) and gates the debrief at n19 (gap 13), and refund_units resurfaces in the status email at n15. The cross-book mid value (claim_score from the card_games book, birdsql:371) is woven into the sla_hours arithmetic and thus into the whole downstream; n20 (formula_1, birdsql:863) is an independent side anchor no downstream check reads. The severity tier re-derived at n12 is TYPE-C — never written to answers, so the agent must recompute it from the live card_games book, and the CSM move's composition gate binds the STAMPED tier to that live re-derivation. The four EnterpriseOps beats are judged by the source tasks' own checks, so any order that leaves the same register end-state passes; each beat's register witness is a state gate the next hop reads directly. The reimbursement is COMPENSATABLE: the first (duplicate-patient) payout must be corrected by a matching [DIP-REVERSAL] clawback then the correct payout — the net payer->correct-patient payout == refund_units, and the collateral 'no_naked_delete_of_wrong_payout' forbids removing the wrong row. On the real data delta=29000 mandates the 'HIGH' route (director handoff, no escalation); the FSV accepts the 'HIGH' route complete AND rejects a spurious escalation note or an extra director email on a 'LOW' route.
